ideas.what: Make the exp60 insertion arms honest before T9 reads them. After shards A/B finish, build a parquet (stem,node_id,t,z,y,x) from every divins_dump/<stem>.npz (node_t, node_zyx, restricted to p_id) and run experiments/l2_daughternet/kdn_score with KDS_COORDS=<that parquet> and KDS_ENSEMBLE=both on vitaliineibauer T4. Add CPU arms to tools/trainlab.py: ins35_oof (#35 config, OOF p, threshold 0.5 = the 24 Sep eligible-count calibration of ensemble 0.4; 0.4 also reported) and ins35_nosteal0_oof. The current ins35 / ins35_nosteal0 / ins35_forkmid45 arms are relabelled 'in-sample upper bound'. Lab only; nothing changes in the x138 submission pipeline.
ideas.why_now: Lab defect found today. The lab arms take node p from the kernel's divins dump (tools/trainlab.py node_p_from_divins l.350). The kernel's DIVINS_CALL (tools/build_probe_kernel.py l.321-337) calls score_nodes without model_index, so it uses the mean over all 5 DaughterNet v1 fold models (tools/daughternet.py l.123/129). DaughterNet v1 was trained on all 199 train videos (CONTEXT l.1275), so every lab clip was seen by 4 of the 5 models. This is the same in-sample trap as the edge filter (+0.016 lab, 0 on LB). OOF and ensemble p differ measurably: p_par 99th percentile 0.90 vs 0.83 (CONTEXT l.1304). T9's 'insertion CONFIRMATION >= 0 per embryo' check and the planned nosteal0 mechanism test both lean on DaughterNet confidence, which T9 itself says to discount to 0. The v3 schedule verifier flagged this for a hypothetical lab (v_metric-math_div-budget-ladder-x138_schedule.notes.md l.7), but exp60 was built without the fix. The dumps already hold the coordinates, so rerunning exp60 is not needed.
ideas.evidence: tools/trainlab.py l.1-35, 350-380; tools/build_probe_kernel.py l.321-337; tools/daughternet.py l.115-129; tools/div_insert.py dump_arrays l.333-372 (node_t, node_zyx, p_id stored); experiments/l2_daughternet/kdn_score/kds_core.py l.1-35, 128-131, 391 (OOF by fold with leak-group audit; any parquet via KDS_COORDS); CONTEXT.md l.1275-1330 (v1 trained on 199 in 5 folds; OOF 0.5 ~ ens 0.4). Prior on nosteal0: in exp39, 15 of 43 FP forks had a wrong ILP-side edge that was often edge_prob 0.0, and the 'drop the 0.0 side' rule fixed 10 FP edges vs 1 TP (research/wf_ideas_v2/r1_research_fork-midpoint-filter.json). Stealing from 0.0 edges is therefore likely the GOOD steal, and nosteal0 is expected to be <= 0.
ideas.expected_gain: 0 on LB directly. It protects the decisions. Without it, the in-sample arms bias toward 'insertion is harmless' and toward whichever steal variant inserts more. A wrong nosteal0 adoption would cost ~1 public event (-0.001). Guard value is about +0.0001..+0.0003 in expectation.
ideas.runtime_cost: 0 on the hidden run (lab only). About 0.3-0.5 GPU-h on Kaggle. The K2 dummy scored 32k nodes in 298 s with 5 models; OOF uses 1 model per clip, and 56 clips hold roughly 0.3-0.5M candidate nodes (guess).
ideas.test_gate: Contract: the ens p recomputed by kdn_score must equal the dump p for every p_id (max |dp| <= 1e-4); otherwise stop and read the ins arms as missing. OOF audit: 0 leak-group violations. Pre-registered reading, written in CONTEXT before the arms are opened: (a) the insertion harm check uses ins35_oof and needs CONFIRMATION >= control - 0.0005 on each embryo. (b) nosteal0 becomes a K-rider only if ins35_nosteal0_oof - ins35_oof >= +2 net evaluable TP over all 56 clips, the in-sample arm agrees in sign, and adj_edge moves by <= 0.0005. Otherwise keep the #35 config (R2) and close nosteal0.
ideas.effort_hours: 1.5-2 (parquet builder ~0.5 h, kdn-score push/pull ~0.5 h, two trainlab arms + test ~0.5-1 h)
ideas.risk: Low. Lab only. Main risk: the dump coordinates are head-refined floats while kdn_score rounds them differently, so the contract check fails. Then the arms stay 'in-sample, discount to 0' as today. No effect on K2/K3 builds.

ideas.what: Re-pre-register the T9 forkmid (C04) audit as a POWERED harm test before any exp60 result is downloaded, and log it in CONTEXT with a timestamp. Pool all 56 lab clips, since forkmid has no parameter chosen on the lab: 4.5 um was fixed from exp39, so the SELECTION/CONFIRMATION split adds nothing here. Gate: (a) 0 TP safe-division forks removed, pooled; (b) max TP-fork mid on x138 coordinates <= 3.8 um (margin >= 0.7 um); (c) removed evaluable FP >= 1 and removed FP > removed TP; (d) pooled adj_edge change >= -0.0002, since the dropped ILP-side 0.0 edge can be a real continuation; (e) node set and inserted-fork counts unchanged. Drop '>= 3 FP with >= 1 on 44b6'. K3 = K2 + forkmid is then judged by R3 on the LB (public >= K2 - 0.001).
ideas.why_now: The current gate (TASK_CLOUD_SESSION.md l.174: >= 3 FP removed, >= 1 on 44b6) is almost unpassable for lack of events, whatever forkmid is worth. Scaling the exp39 audit (2,014 forks: 43 FP / 23 TP evaluable; mid >= 4.5 removes 6 FP / 0 TP, <= 1 of 10 FP on 44b6) to the lab (44b6 11 + 6bba 88 GT divisions; experiments/exp60_trainlab/split.json) and to x138's lower dose (2/62 forks = 3.2% on the dummies, head-refined coordinates) gives expected FP removals of lambda_total ~1.5-3.0 and lambda_44b6 ~0.1-0.4. P(>= 3 total) is 0.19-0.58, P(>= 1 on 44b6) 0.10-0.33, joint ~0.02-0.19 (central ~0.08). The plan assumes P(audit passed) ~0.6. As written, K3 in S4 would almost surely not ship, and the only division rider with a positive-sign prior (+0.0005 public) would be lost to power, not to evidence.

ideas.what: Replace the K3b (DeepCenter safe-division threshold t*) acceptance rule with a marginal-fork precision test, pre-registered before the exp60 results. On the 6bba lab clips, M(t) = the forks that differ between t and 0.25 (added when t < 0.25, removed when t > 0.25). The direction (lower vs higher) is chosen on 6bba SELECTION by the sign of the pooled delta. On 6bba CONFIRMATION, require: >= 6 evaluable marginal forks (TP + FP), and a Wilson 80% lower bound of marginal precision > 0.265 (public break-even J/(1+J) at J 0.36) when forks are added, or an upper bound < 0.167 (private break-even at J ~0.2) when forks are removed. Also require 44b6 delta >= -0.0005, adj_edge within +-0.0005, and the node set unchanged. If it passes, K3b is an F2-variant candidate by R4 only.
ideas.why_now: The plan's K3b gate (6bba CONFIRMATION >= control + 0.002, neighbours >= +0.001) passes on about ONE event. 6bba CONFIRMATION has 45 GT divisions (split.json) and D ~53, so one net TP is +0.0019. The 'plateau' arms are nested fork sets sharing the same events, so they add no independent evidence. Two biases also push the lab toward MORE forks. First, lab J ~0.12 gives a break-even precision of 0.107, against 0.265 on public and ~0.17 on private: a marginal fork at 20% precision 'wins' in the lab and loses on public. Second, the x138 detector saw all 199 train clips, so the lab candidate pool is cleaner than on hidden embryos. Separately, DeepCenter's checkpoint (epoch 2, best_score -0.045) was selected on the 6bba val split (browser_intel.md l.296), so 6bba is not perfectly clean for it. DC vetoes ~87% of geometric candidates (K2 dummy log: rejected 135/210/86/9 vs post-veto 6/20/37/5), so a threshold move changes many forks, of which only ~3% are evaluable (exp39: 66 of 2,014).

Wilson 80% lower bounds: 3/6 0.27, 5/10 0.31, 6/12 0.33, 8/14 0.40.

Under the current gate P(false pass) is ~0.25-0.35 when the true marginal precision is at or below break-even, and a false pass costs -0.001..-0.002 public (1-2 events) and a coin flip on private. Guard EV is ~+0.0002..+0.0005. If DC really leaves precision on the table, P(pass) ~0.10-0.15, with a center of +0.001 public when it passes.
ideas.runtime_cost: 0 (the threshold changes only which candidates pass; DC is already computed)

ideas.what: Optional K3 rider with an output identical to K2 (checked by sha256 on the dummies). (1) Exact two-stage DaughterNet scoring inside DIVINS_CALL: first score only the unique parents u of candidate_triples, then score c1/v only for triples with p_par(u) >= DIVINS_THRESH. This is exact because score = p_par(u) * p_dau(v) * p_dau(c1)^alpha <= p_par(u) when alpha = 1 and p <= 1, so a pruned triple can never be eligible. (2) Raise DIVINS_DEADLINE_S from 28,800 (8.0 h) to 34,200 (9.5 h) to match REPAIR_DEADLINE_S. The Kaggle limit is 12 h, and after 9.5 h all clips degrade quickly, so at most one clip in flight runs full insertion past the gate.
ideas.why_now: New facts: the limit is 12 h, not 9 h, and step 0 puts K2 at <= ~7.8 h against the 8.0 h insertion gate, a worst-case margin of only ~0.2 h. Insertion is the costliest division stage, about 66-75 s/clip, and most of that time scores nodes that can never be inserted. On the K2 dummy, 32,288 nodes were scored for 12 insertions. 44b6_0b24845f spent 65 s scoring 6,988 nodes with 0 eligible. 6bba_05db0fb1 spent 185 s for 142 eligible, of which the cap took 4. If private clips are slower, insertion would silently be skipped on the last clips, losing part of the only division gain that is confirmed on the LB (+0.001).

It also frees ~0.8-1.4 h of hidden runtime (guess: parents are ~1/3 of scored nodes and few pass p_par >= 0.4) for other riders.
ideas.runtime_cost: Negative: about -0.8..-1.4 h on ~100 hidden clips (guess). The deadline change costs at most one clip's insertion (~5 min) past 9.5 h, well under 12 h.
ideas.test_gate: Dummy twin K2 + D4 with FORKMID off: sha256(submission.csv) == K2 dummy, identical per-clip 'added=... (orphan, steal)' log lines, and divins_nodes_scored down >= 50%. Any mismatch (for example cuDNN batch-shape float drift at the 0.4 edge) drops the rider without debugging. FD/FF-style gates are unchanged (the fail-soft wrapper already covers the new code).
ideas.effort_hours: 2-3 (patch in build_probe_kernel.py DIVINS_CALL + unit test on the exactness bound + one dummy ~25 min GPU)
ideas.risk: Lowest priority, and optional: skip it if agent hours are short. The risk is new code in the final, where an exception means 'DIVINS FAILED' and the +0.001 is lost on that clip. Fail-soft limits the damage, but the EV is tiny. Never ship it without the sha256 identity.

plan_critique: Under the divisions lens the v3 plan needs four changes, all doable before the exp60 results arrive (shard A pushed 17:15 UTC). (1) The forkmid (C04) audit gate in TASK_CLOUD_SESSION T9 ('>= 3 FP removed, >= 1 on 44b6') has P(pass) ~0.02-0.19 (central ~0.08) because there are too few events: 44b6 has 11 lab GT divisions and ~0.1-0.4 expected FP removals. The plan's 'P(audit passed) ~0.6' is wrong. Pre-register a pooled harm-only gate (D2) or accept that K3/S4 will not ship. (2) The K3b DeepCenter gate passes on ~1 net TP event (+0.0019 at D ~53 on 6bba CONFIRMATION), and its plateau arms are nested. Lab J ~0.12 puts break-even precision at 0.107 vs 0.265 on public, and the in-sample x138 detector cleans the pool, so the lab favours lowering t. Judge it by marginal-fork precision (D3). Expect it not to ship. (3) The exp60 insertion arms are in-sample for DaughterNet: the kernel's 5-fold mean, where 4 of 5 folds trained on each clip. T9's insertion check and the ins35_nosteal0 comparison must use OOF p (D1). The prior already says nosteal0 is <= 0, because 0.0-prob edges are the wrong side in 15/43 exp39 FP forks, so do not build a nosteal0 K on in-sample evidence. (4) Remove from the lens: DaughterNet fold-ensemble variants (no honest test exists, since each train clip is OOF for exactly one fold, so it would be an LB ladder); sister symmetry (already in x138 safe-div, SAFE_DIV_SISTER_SYMMETRY_TAU 0.6, and untestable for insertion on ~7 evaluable lab events); pre-short-track insertion (a node-set change, so R4, at most 6.6% of GT divisions); cap/threshold changes (ladders). Size of what is left: #35's +0.001 is ~1 net public event. The rest of the division term is forkmid ~+0.0005, plus the DC threshold, which will most likely not ship. Cap agent time on divisions at ~3-4 h (D1-D3) and put the remaining hours into consolidation and finals hygiene. R2/R3/R4 and the §f finals rule stay as written. Optional D4: the 8.0 h insertion gate is now the tightest runtime constraint under the 12 h limit, and an exact p_par prefilter plus a 9.5 h gate removes it at ~0 risk if the dummy sha256 matches.
